388087.title: Orientation of nonideal clutters
388087.outcome: REFUTED (candidate): explicit nonideal (in fact minimally nonideal) clutter on 11 elements with no Kiraly functions (p,q)

exact_statement_restored.egres_text: Let C be a clutter on ground set V, and let B be its blocker. Is it true that C is nonideal if and only if there exist p:C->V and q:B->V such that p(X) in X for every X in C, p(Y) in Y [sic; q(Y)] for every Y in B, if p(X)=q(Y) then |X cap Y|>1?
exact_statement_restored.egres_typo: 'p(Y) in Y' is a typo for 'q(Y) in Y': Pap TR-2010-09 Conjecture 1.2 (single h on C cup B with h(X) in X) and Pap PhD thesis Conjecture 3.4.5 (ii) 'q(B) in B'. A reading with q unconstrained is degenerate: the ideal path clutter {01,12} then admits (p,q), contradicting the proved direction (thesis Thm 3.3.22).
exact_statement_restored.known_direction: ideal => no (p,q): Kiraly-Pap via polyhedral Sperner lemma (Pap thesis Theorem 3.3.22). Open direction: nonideal => (p,q) exists.
exact_statement_restored.definitions: clutter = pairwise incomparable family; blocker = inclusion-minimal transversals; ideal = covering polyhedron {x>=0 : x(X)>=1 for X in C} is integral (all extreme points integral)

counterexample.structure: rows of a cubic (11,3,4) Lehman matrix with k=rs-n=1 (A Bbar^T = J+I after permutation; runs/lehman-structure-n11-1.txt); obtained from the Moebius ladder C_5^3 by two 3-rung ladder insertions (Mayhew-Pivotto-Royle construction); one of the 4 isomorphism classes of (11,3,4) Lehman matrices; core is NOT cyclic (the cyclic one, C_11^3, satisfies the conjecture, as Pap proved); A is isomorphic to A^T
counterexample.blocker: 36 minimal transversals: 11 four-sets (Lehman core) and 25 five-sets; listed in runs/cert-n11-1.json and in the Lean file (YL)
counterexample.nonideal_certificate: x* = (1/3,...,1/3) is an extreme point of P(C): the 11 edge constraints are tight and force x=x*
counterexample.no_pq_certificate: for every choice p(X) in X (3^11 choices) some blocker member Y has every v in Y 'killed' (exists X with X cap Y={v}, p(X)=v), so q(Y) cannot be chosen; encoded as a 6517-leaf case tree checked by the Lean kernel
counterexample.minimally_nonideal: yes (exact diagnostic, not in Lean): exact vertex enumeration finds 37 vertices of P(C) (36 blocker members + x*), and all 22 single-element deletions/contractions are ideal (runs/check-mni-n11-1.txt). Consistent with Mayhew-Pivotto-Royle Table 3 (all four (11,3,4) cubic Lehman matrices are mni).

verification.solver_2_independent: scripts/verify_independent.py: separate blocker code, brute force over all 3^11 p, q decoupled per Y: exists_pq=false [runs/verify-independent-n11.txt]
verification.sanity: both directions validated on known instances: F7, C5^2, C7^2, C9^2, C5^3, C8^3, C11^3, J3, OK5 admit (p,q) (witnesses verified); ideal path, C4, C6, Q6, single edge admit none [runs/sanity.txt]

388146.title: Expected number of copies of sigma in a random tau-avoiding permutation
388146.exact_statement_restored: Cooper, Combinatorial Problems I Like (fetched 2026-11-01T04:18:18Z, sha256 ba547f05...5a): 'Given two permutations sigma and tau, what is the expected number of copies of sigma in a permutation chosen uniformly at random from those permutations on n symbols which avoid tau?' Random model: uniform on Av_n(tau); quantity E_n(sigma,tau) = (sum over pi in Av_n(tau) of #occurrences of sigma in pi)/|Av_n(tau)|; quantifiers: all sigma, tau, all n (exact) - no asymptotic regime specified.
388146.outcome: NO ENDPOINT: source-based intractability of a complete answer
388146.barrier: For sigma of length k, E_k(sigma,tau) = [sigma avoids tau]/|Av_k(tau)|. Hence a complete answer for all (sigma,tau,n) contains the exact enumeration |Av_n(tau)| for every tau, in particular tau=1324, a well-known open enumeration problem (no formula, growth rate unknown). For fixed (sigma,tau,n) the value is a finite rational computation (tautological). Published partial answers: Bona 2010 (arXiv:0910.1343, DMTCS) for tau=132 / monotone sigma, Homberger 2012 (EJC 19(3) P43) for all length-3 sigma in Av_n(123).

388171.title: Supremum R of reciprocal sums of (strongly) sum-free sets
388171.exact_statement_restored: Cooper (same fetch): S subset of positive integers, no element equals the sum of a nonempty set of OTHER (distinct) elements; R = sup over such S of sum_{s in S} 1/s. Same object as Erdos Problem #876's secondary question (erdosproblems.com/876, fetched 2026-11-01T04:18:17Z, sha256 c9e9f547...de41: 'determine the maximum possible value of sum 1/n'). Known 2.0649 < R < 3.9998 (Levine-O'Sullivan chi-inequality upper bound; Abbott 1987/Zhang 1992 lower bounds; attributions as on MathWorld/Wikipedia; Cooper's text swaps them); Levine-O'Sullivan conjecture R ~ 3.01.
388171.outcome: NO ENDPOINT: determining R exactly is an open problem since Erdos 1962 / Levine-O'Sullivan 1977; no finite certificate can determine a supremum over infinite sets without a new structural theorem; erdosproblems.com shows 2 'proof claims' that I did not read or assess.
